structured_output.what_is_happening: A roughly 58-day-old Pump.fun token that has graduated to PumpSwap (Cog, "cat-dog" meme, $118k mcap, $41k liquidity) triggered the rule on a single short volume burst. About $1.6k of volume in 5–15 minutes pushed price up about 13%. The hour saw 866 buys from 828 unique buyers averaging about $1.30 per buy, which fits automated micro-buy or holder-inflation bots more than organic demand. GeckoTerminal shows only $0.45 of volume in the most recent 5 minutes, so the burst has already stopped. There is a paid DexScreener boost.

narrative.description: Generic 'cat-dog hybrid from a viral video' meme with a website, X and Telegram. It is presented as a long-term community meme brand, but no fresh catalyst shows up in the packet.
narrative.why_spreading: No evidence of organic spread. The activity looks like bot micro-transactions plus a paid DexScreener boost, not new social attention. Price change over 6h is only about +2%, and the token is about 5.5x below its all-time-high price.

token_connection.why_this_token: The name, X handle (CogTheCatDog), website and Telegram all match this contract. It is by far the most liquid and active COG/cog token.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 8 other COG/cog tickers, including 'cat dog' and 'Cog' clones launched recently (pair creation around 1790027000–1790038000 ms). All are near-zero liquidity with no volume.

authenticity.evidence: Hourly volume of about $1,780 spread over 866 buys by 828 unique buyers (about $1–2 per buy) is a textbook sign of micro-buy bots. The 24h figures are similar: 8,969 trades for $32.7k. GMGN bundler_wallets and fresh_wallets both sit at the 1,000 cap. Holder counts don't match: 4,993 (RugCheck) vs 908–917 (GMGN and GeckoTerminal). A paid DexScreener boost is active. RugCheck found insider transfer networks of 8 and 6 wallets. The creator has launched 27 tokens.
authenticity.uncertainty: The wallet-tag caps may be classification artifacts. The micro-buys could come from a community raid tool rather than the team. With no X data, I can't rule out a real social catalyst.

structural_risks: Very thin real volume: about $1.6k moves price by double digits
Paid boost can create a short spike that reverses
About 44% held by top 10 per GeckoTerminal (including pool and lockers)

structured_output.counterargument: The contract is clean: mint and freeze authority renounced, liquidity pool fully burned or locked, about 9% locked in Streamflow, no tax, and creator holdings near 1%. The token has survived about 2 months with $41k liquidity, a maintained website and socials, and 124 smart and 11 renowned wallets among past traders. An active community with a paid boost could turn a small low-float move into a real bounce toward earlier highs, especially since price is far below its all-time high and little volume is needed to move it.
unknowns: What is being posted on X or Telegram, and whether there is any real catalyst
Whether the micro-buys come from the team, a community raid tool or a third-party bot service
Why holder counts differ so much between data sources
Who controls the insider transfer networks

source_coverage.notes: No internet access in this condition. The judgment rests only on the evidence packet.

structured_output.thesis: A short, low-dollar burst on an aging cat-dog meme token, driven by bot-like micro-buys and a paid boost. Real volume is too small to sustain the move, and the most recent 5 minutes are already near zero. I expect it to drift back within hours.
